messages:
maria: ran an nsys perf run on the new batching heuristic, and seeing a regression when batch -> 12. timeline shows matmul switching to a cuBLASLt algo with a ~1.2GB workspace allocation, which triggers KV cache evictions and spikes latency :grimacing:

kevin: can you paste the shape/params? is this the attention qk matmul or the ff matmuls?

maria: qk matmul in decode path. shapes end up as (batch_heads=192, seq=4096, head_dim=64) after packing for decode (so GEMM roughly 192x64 x 64x4096 depending on layout). before the switch, we used algo 5 with small workspace ~64MB. nsys snippet:
```
cudaProfiler Start -> matmul: cublasLtAlgo 23 workspace=1203MB time=46.9ms
previously: cublasLtAlgo 5 workspace=64MB time=31.2ms
```

devon: ouch. 1.2GB workspace per op will kill any real batch. do we have the full kernel timeline? perfetto or the nsys capture link helps. perf-bot?

perf-bot: trace uploaded -> https://perf.redwood.local/trace/1762509876 (expires in 7d) :white_check_mark:

aaron: two quick possibilities: 1) cuBLASLt auto-tuner picked an algorithm optimized for throughput but with huge workspace; 2) our algo selection heuristic is accidentally favoring large-workspace choices for certain stride/padding combos.

kevin: also check alignment/padding. cuBLASLt will choose tensor-core friendly algos only if dims align to 8/16. small misalignment sometimes flips to a slow but high-workspace algo.

maria: yeah alignment looks fine. I dumped the cublasLt algo descriptor from the run:
```
AlgoDesc(id=23, tile=128x128x8, epilogue=RELU, uses_split_k=false, workspace=1258291200)
```

devon: that epilogue=RELU is weird for pure GEMM in attention — suggests our call site is reusing a matmul wrapper that sets epilogue flags. Could be activating fused ops which changes algorithm space.

aaron: good catch. if we accidentally request fused bias/gelu or epilogue, cublasLt expands algorithm choices. check our wrapper: rdl/runtime/kernels/matmul_wrapper.cu — any epilogue flags for decode path?

maria: wrapper had epilogue=ADD_BIAS in one code path (meant for FFN), and decode path sometimes hits it because we reuse the same descriptor when head_dim!=kv_head_dim. simple bug. repro patch attached.

kevin: mitigation options: 1) quick patch: force epilogue=NULL for attention path; 2) set a workspace cap in our cublasLt query to reject >128MB algos; 3) add a metric in Console to alert when chosen workspace > X.

devon: option 2 is safest short-term. cublasLt supports returning a list of algos; we can filter by workspace before selecting. snippet I used previously:
```py
algos = cublasLt.find_algos(desc)
filtered = [a for a in algos if a.workspace_bytes <= 128*1024*1024]
choose_best(filtered)
```

maria: trying that locally now. also verifying KV cache eviction sequence: when workspace spikes, device memory goes from 80%->>100% and we start evicting cached KV pages; that causes extra host<->device copies and explodes latency. nsys timeline shows devmem alloc/free around the matmul spike.

perf-bot: note added: incident #IR-2026-119 - transient decode latency regression caused by large cuBLASLt workspace selection. tagged eng-runtime, eng-ml.

aaron: long-term: we should add a "workspace budget" per model instance and prefer algos that keep total device working set under budget. also consider fallback to cuBLAS (non-Lt) for pathological shapes — often smaller workspace but acceptable perf.

kevin: can we also log the selected algo id + workspace in traces automatically? even a small tag in metrics would speed root cause next time.

maria: agreed. opened PR with 1) forced epilogue-null for attention path, 2) workspace-filter in algo selection, 3) trace tag for algo_id/workspace. testing on a 24hr replay job now.

devon: nice. once PR is up, run the perf test matrix across seq lengths {512,1024,2048,4096} and batch sizes {4,8,12,16} to ensure no regressions for small batches.

maria: will do. preliminary local results: regression gone for batch<=16, and KV cache stable. pushing to CI full matrix.

aaron: FYI: add a unit that simulates prefilled KV cache memory pressure so CI can catch this class of issues early.

kevin: thanks for the quick catch. lesson: fused epilogue + auto-tuner combo can be a perf footgun. :hammer_and_wrench:

maria: thanks all — will update thread when CI finishes (should be ~15m).
